correctness.rationale: The recurrence yields c=q b-a, gcd(a,b)=1, b>2a and q<a, with r in {1,q-1}. The reductions q b→a+c and (Q+1)c→(b-Q-1)a+(q-r)b together with the third trade generate a unique canonical factorization where (y,z) enumerate t=y+qz in [0,a-1]; coprimality then forces unique x. At each of the three Betti degrees, explicit divisibility bounds show exactly the two factorizations in RESULT.md, with disjoint supports. Trade distances yield the upper bound D=b-Q+q-r-1; the two-factor E_C fiber forces the same lower bound. The 4-cycle of odd-index Pell residues modulo q proves the stated mod-eight branches. Independent integer checks verified 60 parameter pairs and bounded critical fibers; those are corroboration, not all-parameter proof.

final_claim: For u>=1 and odd i>=5, the numerical semigroup generated by consecutive odd-index steps a=P_i(u), b=P_(i+2)(u), c=P_(i+4)(u) has exactly three indispensable stated Betti trades. Its catenary degree is b-Q+q-r-1 for q=u^2+2, Q=floor(a/q), r=a mod q; r=1 for i=1,7 mod8 and r=q-1 for i=3,5 mod8, giving an exact two-branch mod-eight law.
